prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1409; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road and said the other vehicle drifted into their lane. Claimant states a wrist fracture resulted and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. The responding officer's notes match the described impact point.

Entry 3: Photos of the claimant's vehicle show side damage consistent with the reported contact. The other driver gave a statement that agrees with the claimant's version of the lane change.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses at the scene described the sideswipe the same way the claimant did. Claimant has repeated the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Confirmed the driver listed on the policy is the person who was operating the vehicle. No prior damage to the vehicle is on file, although a neighbor believes the car had been hit some weeks before the reported date. Following up on that statement.

Entry 6: Medical records show a wrist fracture with treatment that followed a usual course and tapered as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same area appears in the history provided. Causal link to this collision is still under review.

Entry 7: Repair estimate lines up with the damage pattern shown in the photos and the reported impact. Neighbor follow-up is pending to clarify the timing of the earlier damage they described.

Entry 8: File remains open. Causation of the wrist injury is not yet confirmed. Next step is to obtain the treating provider's opinion on whether the fracture is consistent with this collision.
